cases.situation: I'm a freelance email copywriter. Found a skincare brand, Fern & Salt, whose welcome email is just a discount code. Want to pitch the founder, Olivia.
cases.reply:
Subject: Fern & Salt's welcome email

Hi Olivia,
I signed up last week and your welcome email is a single 10% code, with none of the seaweed-sourcing story that makes your product pages so good. I write welcome sequences for skincare brands; the last one, for Kind Botanics, lifted first-order rate from 3.1% to 5.4%. Want a two-line idea for yours? If it's not relevant, a 'no' is genuinely useful.
Tom

cases.situation: J'anime des ateliers de céramique à Lyon. Je veux proposer une collab à Claire, une créatrice Instagram (30k abonnés) qui fait des vidéos sur les loisirs créatifs lents.
cases.reply: Bonjour Claire, ta vidéo sur le tricot comme pause anti-écran m'a vraiment parlé, c'est exactement l'esprit de nos ateliers de céramique à Lyon. Trois créatrices lyonnaises ont déjà filmé une séance chez nous, la dernière vidéo a fait 80 000 vues. J'ai une idée simple, avec un atelier offert pour toi et une amie. Je te l'explique en deux lignes ?
cases.note: Le « pourquoi toi » d'abord, une preuve chiffrée, puis une toute petite demande.

cases.situation: Emailed the head of People at a 200-person company about our onboarding software a week ago. No reply. Want to follow up once with something actually useful.
cases.reply: Hi Grace, bumping this with one more thing: we just published a two-page checklist on cutting first-week IT tickets, based on 40 mid-size rollouts. It's attached and free to use whether or not we ever talk. No pressure on the original ask.
cases.note: Follow-up 1 adds value instead of 'just checking in'. One more after a week, then stop.

cases.situation: 我做餐饮门店的排班软件销售，给一家连锁火锅店的IT负责人郑先生发过一封冷邮件、跟进过一次。今天他回了一句：“你们已经发了好几次了，别再给我发了。”
cases.reply: 好的，郑先生，已经把您从我们所有的发送名单里移除了，打扰了。
cases.note: 对方语气冲，就只回一次：确认已删除、道一句歉，不解释、不再推销，然后真的从所有名单里删掉。

cases.situation: I'm a backend engineer looking for my next job. Rachel Okafor, an engineering manager at Loomly, wrote a great LinkedIn post about moving their job queue off Postgres. They have no open roles listed. I want to message her.
cases.reply: Hi Rachel, your post on moving Loomly's job queue off Postgres was the clearest write-up of that trade-off I've read this year. I'm a backend engineer; at Parcelwise I led a similar migration to SQS that cut p95 job latency from 40 seconds to 3. Is your team hiring backend engineers in the next few months? A quick yes or no is genuinely helpful.
cases.note: A job search is still cold outreach: prove you read her work, give one number, and ask a yes/no question instead of asking for a call.

cases.situation: I coach an under-10s football team, the Riverside Robins. We need new kits, about £600 for 18 kids. There's a family bakery on our high street, Crumb & Co, and the owner Sophie posts a lot about supporting local things. I want to DM her on Instagram.
cases.reply: Hi Sophie, I coach the Riverside Robins, the under-10s who play on Harlow Rec every Saturday morning, just up the road from you. We're looking for a local sponsor for new kits this season: £600 covers shirts for all 18 kids, with Crumb & Co on the front. Last season's sponsor, Park Lane Cycles, told us the Saturday crowd of parents was their best local advertising. Would you be open to it? A no is completely fine too.
cases.note: Exact cost, what she gets, one piece of proof, one yes/no question. The easy no matters more when you're asking a neighbourhood business.

cases.situation: I run a volunteer repair café in Bristol; we've fixed 1,240 items this year. Amy Clarke at the Bristol Post wrote last week about households binning broken appliances because repair costs more than buying new. I want to email her.
cases.reply:
Subject: 1,240 things Bristol didn't throw away

Hi Amy,
Your piece last week on people binning appliances because repair costs more than new is exactly what we see every month. We run a free volunteer repair café in Easton and have fixed 1,240 items since January, mostly lamps, kettles and toasters. Happy to send the month-by-month numbers, no strings. Useful for a follow-up? A quick no is helpful too.
Sam
cases.note: Press pitch: tie it to her own story, give one number, and offer her something usable instead of asking for coverage.

cases.situation: 我做企业管理培训。上周给一家物流公司的HR总监周女士发了私信，推荐我们的新任主管培训课。她回复：“今年预算已经定了，明年再说吧。”
cases.reply: 谢谢周总直接回复我，这对我很有帮助。想问一下，贵司明年大概几月开始定培训预算？我到时候再联系您，在那之前就不打扰了。
cases.note: 对方说“不是现在”，就问清楚什么时候，记个提醒，然后真的等到那时再联系，中间不要“顺便问问”。

cases.situation: I'm a sports dietitian and want to pitch myself as a guest to Tom Reyes, who hosts a mid-size running podcast, Long Run Home. On his episode last month he said he wished someone would explain race-day fueling properly.
cases.reply:
Subject: Guest idea: why marathoners hit the wall at mile 20

Hi Tom, at the end of your episode with the Boston 3:05 runner last month, you said you wished someone would explain race-day fueling properly. I'm a sports dietitian and I've worked with over 300 marathoners on exactly that; most of their problems come down to one timing mistake. Would a 30-minute episode on it fit your spring lineup? If it's not a fit, a quick 'no' is genuinely helpful.
Lena Park, RD
cases.note: Podcast pitch: his own words as the why-you, one line of proof, and a yes-or-no ask about the show rather than a call.

cases.situation: I sell route-planning software to logistics companies. Emailed Ben, ops director at Northgate Freight, on Sept 15, then followed up Sept 22 with a case study. Nothing back. I want to send the last one.
cases.reply: Hi Ben, last note from me on this. If route planning isn't a priority for Northgate right now, no worries at all, and I'll leave it here. If it becomes one, the Halden Freight numbers (11% fewer miles in their first quarter) will still be on our site. Door's open.
cases.note: The final follow-up is short, carries no guilt, leaves one reason to come back later, and then you actually stop.

cases.situation: I run a 3,000-member Slack group for indie bookshop owners. I cold-DMed Hannah, who writes the Shelf Life newsletter about bookselling, asking if she'd hear a two-line idea for a joint piece. She replied: 'Sure, what's the idea?'
cases.reply: Thanks, Hannah. The idea: a short survey of our 3,000 members on how they price secondhand books, with the results published first in Shelf Life in November. We'd write and run the survey; you'd only need to share the link once. Interested?
cases.note: Once they say 'go on', keep the promise you made: two lines, what it costs them, and a yes/no question.

cases.situation: I'm a second-year engineering student and want summer research experience. Professor Kenji Nakamura in the marine science department wrote a 2025 paper on low-cost temperature loggers for reef monitoring. I built a similar logger in my embedded systems class. I've never emailed a professor cold.
cases.reply:
Subject: Your reef temperature logger paper

Hi Professor Nakamura,
Your 2025 paper on low-cost loggers for reef monitoring is the reason I added a marine science minor. I'm a second-year engineering student, and last spring I built and calibrated a similar logger for my embedded systems class, accurate to 0.1°C in our tank tests. Would you consider taking an undergraduate volunteer in your lab this summer? If there's no room, a quick no is genuinely helpful.
Best,
Aisha Rahman
cases.note: Student to professor: prove you read their work, show one thing you've built, and ask a single yes/no question.

cases.situation: 我是一家做宠物医院管理系统的创业公司的CTO，想招一位后端负责人。GitHub上有个开发者“林工”维护一个开源排班库，我们自己一直在用，他上个月刚修了一个跨时区的bug。想在他主页留的邮箱给他发封信。
cases.reply:
标题：你的排班库，和一个后端负责人的位置

林工你好，我们团队一直在用你维护的排班库，上个月你修的跨时区bug正好解决了我们线上的一个问题。我们做宠物医院管理系统，现在全国有1,200家诊所在用，正在找一位后端负责人，年薪40万到55万。想问一下，你最近对新机会开放吗？不考虑的话，回一句“不用”也很有帮助。
cases.note: 招人也是冷启动私信：先证明你真用过他的东西，给一个数字和薪资范围，只问一个是或否的问题。

cases.situation: I'm raising a $600k pre-seed round for an app that helps small breweries track their kegs. Angel investor Dana Whitfield backed Canlift, another brewery tool, and wrote a blog post in July calling keg loss an unsolved problem. Canlift's founder, Tom Alvarez, said I can mention him.
cases.reply:
Subject: Keg tracking, via Tom at Canlift

Hi Dana,
Tom Alvarez at Canlift suggested I write to you. Your July post called keg loss the brewing problem nobody has solved; we track every keg with a $4 tag and a phone scan. The 23 breweries in our pilot have cut lost kegs by 60% in four months. We're raising a $600k pre-seed. Would you be open to a one-page summary? A 'no' is genuinely helpful too.
Mia Okonkwo
cases.note: Investor pitch: lead with the referral and her own words, one number, and ask to send a one-pager, not for a meeting.
